301	### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right
302	
303	- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
304	- **Boot check at the freeze:** every handle name in the kernel's issued-handle table corresponds to a subscription registered as `INPUT_SURFACE` with the same name; a handle issued to a name with no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails boot. This ties ADR-0002's table to this ADR's class (ADR-0004's `subscribe` carries the diagnostic name as its `name` argument).
305	- **Where a submit call may occur.** An `INPUT_SURFACE` object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` submits from **its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`**, exactly as the Input Adapter does (ADR-0001 § 2 already lets any registered INPUT_SURFACE node run below `TICK_DRIVER`, and § 3 puts the Adapter there). A UI surface (Chart Table menus later, the Interaction prompt if it ever submits) **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits it from that `_process`, so its commands are queued before the driver's tick loop and reach the same tick as the Adapter's. It **never** calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object (ADR-0001 guideline restated). The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal. This ADR therefore adds no second submit location and no driver stage for submission.
306	- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's own presenter step (the stage it is registered for), never in the handler.
307	- **The rule is per object, not per system** (CR-10): a HUD that grows a button splits into the HUD presenter (`PRESENTATION`) and a small `INPUT_SURFACE` intent object.
308	- Presentation predicts no outcome; the Adapter's pre-play of body motion and sound keyed by `correlation` is ADR-0019's, and light and effects change only on committed state (kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP).
309	
310	### 8. Engine signals stay inside presentation
311	
312	Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 § 1 decides a kernel-owned observer registry of Callables and no engine signals; this ADR agrees), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.
313	
314	### Key Interfaces
315	
316	```gdscript
317	# ----- Issued by the composition root (ADR-0001 § 5); presentation objects receive only these -----
318	class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted        # see § 1
319	class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted        # ADR-0001: tick_alpha, T, running (+ load_seq, requested)
320	
321	# ----- Handler (kernel-invoked; ADR-0003 callable contract; shape fixed by ADR-0004 § 2) -----
322	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken
323	
324	# ----- Driver (src/presentation/) -----
325	class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted        # constants, § 3
326	class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted      # § 3
327	class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted             # § 3
328	class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted       # register / freeze / frame / notify_camera_cut
329	class_name PresentationHost extends Node               # setup(driver); _process(delta) -> driver.frame(delta, present_time)
330	
331	# ----- Placement (src/presentation/placement.gd) -----
332	class_name Placement extends RefCounted                # at / alpha_n / put, § 4
333	
334	const DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE: int = 0
335	const DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT: int = 1
336	```
337	
338	### Implementation Guidelines
339	- **Must** subscribe through a `PresentationFacet` the composition root issued; **must never** hold the kernel, `SimViews`, a `WriteScope` or a tick-phase `ctx` in `src/presentation/`.
340	- **Must** write a subscriber handler as "mark dirty, copy event scalars, `return ctx.complete()`"; **must never** read a view, touch a node, allocate, emit a signal, `await` or submit in a handler.
341	- **Must** keep `dirty` and `animating` separate; **must never** return early on an empty dirty set while a value is animating.
342	- **Must** perform bulk or structural reads only when the block (or `ALL`) is dirty; scalar getters on the interpolated pair may be read each frame while animating.
343	- **Must** register one `PresenterDescriptor` per system with a stage from `PresentationStage` and a truthful `reads` list; **must never** write a literal stage number, define `_process` in a registered presenter, or read a product of the same or a later stage. The `_process` rule applies to objects registered through a `PresenterDescriptor`; the exemptions are `PresentationHost` (and the Pipeline root that may host it), `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`, and layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (PR-9).
344	- **Must** place every moving thing with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put`; **must never** use `int()`, `round`, `roundi`, a tween, an engine interpolation or any other rounding for a sim-owned position, and **must never** assign `position`, `global_position`, `transform` or `offset` outside `placement.gd`.
345	- **Must** read alpha only from `PresentFrame`; **must never** read `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` in a presenter, extrapolate past 1, or use `T` or a tick counter as cosmetic phase.
346	- **Must** animate sim-visible world and HUD content from `frame.present_time`; **must never** leave a free-running `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` or particle clock on layer 0 or layer 2 content.
347	- **Must** keep `physics/common/physics_interpolation` false, put `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF` on the presentation roots, and pass the post-first-frame boot walk; **must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0001).
348	- **Must** write only the allow-list of § 1; **must never** write `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` outside the Pipeline root and the camera host, and **must never** write a block, a command, a physics body, `SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale` or synthetic input.
349	- **Must** reset every presentation scalar in `on_discontinuity`; **must never** persist, hash, replicate or feed back a presentation scalar, or let one decide a truth-channel element's visibility.
350	- **Must** submit only from an object that is both an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration and a `SurfaceHandle` holder; **must never** call `submit` from a signal handler, `_gui_input`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object, and **must never** infer submit rights from the subscriber class.
351	- **Must** use signals only between presentation objects for user-initiated events; **must never** declare or connect an engine signal in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/`.
352	- **Should** drive the driver with an injected `PresentFrame` in tests (stub presenters, injected `present_time`, no scene); **should** record stage timing only in dev and playtest builds.

522	- **OQ-B. Who publishes the beam pose the rim fringe reads (TR-percfilter-043)?** The AVATAR stage (TR-pc-040) is assumed. If Lighting republishes it, the fringe needs a stage after LIGHTING. Decide with ADR-0028.
523	- **OQ-C. Camera limits ownership.** TR-shipbody-032 says `body.projector` owns `Camera2D.limit_*`; Pipeline C2 says `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at engine defaults and the solver is the only clamp (and the primary variant has no `Camera2D` at all); TR-pxl-017 says the PROJECTOR sets limits "consumed by the solver alone". 524	- **OQ-D. `PresentationClock.load_seq`** (§ 6) is a request to ADR-0001. ADR-0004's draft supplies no restore marker; if ADR-0001 declines, the fallback is a composition-root counter on the clock (R9). One of the two must exist before this ADR is Accepted.
525	- **OQ-E. Which node hosts the driver** (Pipeline root or a node it owns) and where `present_time` is advanced relative to `frame(...)`: ADR-0008.
526	- **OQ-F. The cosmetic hash** (PF-37 requires a pure integer hash with explicit 32-bit masking and no dependence on GDScript integer overflow) belongs with ADR-0005's hash family; the Filter GDD calls it an ADR candidate ("a PRESENTATION-only stream"). This ADR only forbids the global RNG, `RandomNumberGenerator` and `rng_derive` for cosmetics.
527	- **OQ-G. TR-pc-039 wording.** "Presenter frame/position/light logs byte-identical across render cadences" cannot hold for per-frame placements, which vary with alpha by design. The Player Controller GDD should say "per-tick samples".
528	- **OQ-H. The `PERCEPTION_OUT` read rule.** The kernel GDD's CR-10 table lets `PRESENTATION` read `PERCEPTION_OUT` views; `architecture.md` and Principle 3 say Filter and Debug only. This ADR takes the narrower rule and needs two views from `PresentationViews` (default and perception-capable). ADR-0003 § 7 describes one `PresentationViews`; ADR-0024 owns the final split.
529	- **OQ-J. Where the camera solve runs (conflict with ADR-0008 draft, owner ADR-0008).** ADR-0008 § 6.2 and its budget table place `CameraSolver.solve` inside the `frame_pre_draw` handler, after every presentation node has positioned itself. This ADR's CAMERA_SOLVE stage (1) solves in the driver's `_process` pass because the HUD (stage 5) needs `world_to_hud` and the Avatar and camera must share `Placement.at` inputs; only the `canvas_transform` and parallax-offset write may be in `frame_pre_draw`. 530	- **OQ-K. Kernel state for the Pipeline (ADR-0008 assumption A2).** `PresentFrame.running` and `PresentationClock.running` carry a boolean only. The Pipeline's need for `RUNNING`/`PAUSED`/`SAVING`/`LOADING`/`FAULTED` is met by a separate read-only accessor on the Pipeline root's own facet from the composition root (ADR-0001 or ADR-0008), not by widening `PresentationFacet`; this ADR does not add it.

409	- **R1: `frame_pre_draw` ordering fails the pipeline spike** (fires before `_process`, or not in a way the host can use). Mitigation: only the `canvas_transform` write depends on it, and PR-6 C2 already names the fallback (the Pipeline root's own `_process` at the lowest priority, which still precedes the draw). No presenter depends on it.
410	- **R2: Release-export `_process` order differs from the headless probe** (host not after the TickDriver). Mitigation: KRN-LAT-02 is a precondition of Accepting ADR-0001 and therefore of this ADR; the fallback is the sequential-parent design recorded in ADR-0001.
411	- **R3: `Placement.put`'s equality skip is wrong for a node whose transform is also set elsewhere.** Mitigation: the lint makes `placement.gd` the only assignment point, and the post-frame fractional sweep in tests catches a stray writer.
412	- **R4: A presenter forgets to react to a key** (the dirty set is correct but the presenter ignores it). Mitigation: the dirty-correctness equivalence test (`rebuild_signature`) and ADR-0004's debug check; the first catches presenter bugs, the second kernel-side marking bugs.
413	- **R5: 4.7 `CanvasItem` lines lose their antialiasing feather**, which makes any `draw_line` hairline thinner than the art assumed. Mitigation: out of this ADR's decision, but the write allow-list does not make `draw_*` a placement mechanism; instruments use pre-rendered needle frames (TR-instr-010); ADR-0028 and ADR-0030 own the line-drawing consequence.
414	- **R6: A freed presenter or a stale `Callable`** at teardown or scene change. Mitigation: `is_valid()` per call with `PRESENTER_DEAD`; the teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value, as ADR-0003 requires of owners.
415	- **R7: `speed_scale = 0` does not freeze a given particle or animation node.** Mitigation: UNVERIFIED and spike-bound (PRES-SPIKE-1); the fallback is to compute the frame index from `present_time` and not use the engine clock at all for that node.
416	- **R8: The stage list is wrong for a presenter nobody has designed yet** (Interaction prompt art, a future overlay). Mitigation: the stage list is a constants file; adding a stage renumbers nothing that anyone writes by hand (nobody writes a literal) and the `reads` check re-validates the graph at boot.
417	- **R9: The `load_seq` request is declined by ADR-0001's owner.** Mitigation: ADR-0004's draft has no restore marker, so the fallback is a counter bumped by the composition root's load host when `request_restore` or `request_new_game` completes (LOADING to RUNNING), exposed on the same `PresentationClock` object; only the driver consumes it either way. Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by three constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:

```gdscript
class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted

## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush
const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; every presentation node, so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
```

The three-step order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.

Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk**: every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s
- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
- Code in `src/sim/` and `src/presentation/` does not `await get_tree().process_frame` (that signal fires outside the per-node ordering, UNVERIFIED); waiting is expressed in ticks or in `present_time`.

### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`

I notice ADR-0008 contradicts ADR-0009's single-host rule by placing presentation subscribers' processing elsewhere, which ties into open questions OQ-J/L, and also mandates using present_time for layer-0 animation. I'm also flagging that ADR-0001 forbids relying on tree order, yet PipelineRoot and PresentationHost both tie at depth 0 if treated separately — a direct conflict worth tracking across these ADRs.

The better fix seems to be making the PipelineRoot itself the host, advancing present_time within the same _process step before the driver frame, with ADR-0008 owning that amendment. I'm also checking several other cross-ADR consistency points — confirming ADR-0001's rules about awaiting process_frame and process_priority ordering hold up, noting the frame_pre_draw conflict between ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 as high severity, and verifying that load_seq and subscription handling in ADR-0004/ADR-0009 remain compatible.

Moving through a few minor naming and lint checks that turn out fine, I land on ADR-0009's requirement that `present` be a typed Callable taking a single PresentFrame argument — since static typing can't enforce this, I'm recommending a runtime freeze check using `get_argument_count()` and `is_standard()`, consistent with how ADR-0003 already validates callables. I'm also confirming that engine APIs referenced in the "Engine Compatibility" table, like process_priority and RenderingServer's frame callbacks, actually exist in the probed 4.7.2 build.

I'm checking the fractional placement sweep across global_position and Sprite2D's centered/offset modes, confirming float32 precision holds for positions under 2^24, and verifying the previous-tick placement semantics. Then I notice a subtle bias in the floored-lerp interpolation: because floor() rounds toward negative infinity, a sprite moving in the positive direction only reveals its new pixel at alpha=1.0 right as the next tick begins, making positive motion appear one tick delayed, while negative motion snaps to the new pixel almost immediately once alpha exceeds zero — an asymmetric visual lag depending on direction of travel.

This stays internally consistent since every object (camera, sprites, etc.) uses the same floor function, but it does mean relative offsets between objects moving in opposite directions will differ slightly in perceived timing. Since this follows the GDD's PR-4 specification for floor-based placement, I'll flag it as a minor non-blocking note rather than a blocking issue, keeping the validation focused on engine correctness.

I want to quickly double check the ADR's claim that snap flags default to false, along with the interpolation nuance and sibling ordering around frame_pre_draw, with a fast additional probe.

findings.text: Idiomatic and compiles, with no blocking engine defect. One-host-node plus RefCounted presenters registered as Callables is a normal Godot manager pattern. It needs no per-presenter _process, no const of a constructed object and no packed array held by reference. All class_names are free of native clashes (probed with ClassDB.class_exists). Member names on RefCounted classes do not clash with Object methods: name, T, alpha, reads, present, views, clock. If a descriptor ever becomes a Node or Resource, name collides with Node.name. Typed-collection use (Array[int] reads) is fine for literals. Confidence: high (compile and clash checks by reading plus probe; I did not run a parse of the ADR snippets).
findings.amendment: No change required. Optionally add a one-line guideline that presenter descriptors stay RefCounted so name does not collide with Node.name or Resource.resource_name.

findings.text: PresentationDriver.freeze() 'sorts once by stage' with no tie-break. Array.sort_custom is NOT stable in Godot. Probed on 4.7.2: a 40-element array with duplicate keys came back out of insertion order. Stage 0 PROJECT already holds two registrants, the layout projector and Lighting's occluder builder. The occluder builder depends on the tiles the layout projector builds, so a tie would give a nondeterministic order that varies by registration count. ADR-0005 s1.7 already bans sort_custom in src/sim and src/kernel for this reason, but the ban does not cover src/presentation. Confidence: high (probed).
findings.amendment: Sort on a packed integer key, stage * 1024 + registration_index, using plain Array.sort() on ints, as ADR-0005 recommends. Alternatively make the freeze check reject two descriptors in one stage unless one lists the other in reads. In either case split PROJECT into PROJECT_LAYOUT and PROJECT_OCCLUDERS, or declare an intra-stage order, so the occluder builder runs after the layout projector.

findings.text: Probe claims plausibility (the 2026-10-28 headless probes). Checked on 4.7.2 and consistent: SceneTree.physics_interpolation exists; physics/common/physics_interpolation, snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel and snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel all default false; Node2D lacks get_global_transform_interpolated while Node3D has it; frame_pre_draw exists; floori(-3+0.5) = -3; process_priority runs in ascending order. The is_physics_interpolated caveat is also REPRODUCED and is sharper than stated: an INHERIT child under an OFF parent reads true in _initialize and false after the first process_frame, and a child added later reads false immediately. Inheritance propagates lazily, not 'only in a running tree'. Also, is_physics_interpolated() ignores the global enable flag: a default node reads true even with the global setting false (is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled() reads false). That is why the boot walk requires explicit OFF roots, which the ADR does. The ADR's shorthand 'physics_interpolation_mode = OFF' is not valid GDScript. Confidence: high (all re-run by me).
findings.amendment: Write Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF (value 2) in code and prose. Keep the gdUnit4 test that enables SceneTree.physics_interpolation and asserts is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled() is false.

findings.text: The position-write lint and the PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL sweep have engine holes. ADR-0009 solves in CAMERA_SOLVE stage 1 and has one PresentationHost with no presenter _process. These are incompatible. The HUD at stage 5 needs world_to_hud before frame_pre_draw runs. Engine side: frame_pre_draw does fire after all node _process in a windowed 4.7.2 run (probed), so a write-only handler is viable. Confidence: high.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 moves solve to the CAMERA_SOLVE stage and leaves only the canvas_transform and parallax-offset write in the frame_pre_draw handler. It also redraws its diagram as 'PipelineRoot or host._process -> PresentationDriver.frame'.

cross_adr.text: PipelineRoot (advances present_time) and PresentationHost (calls driver.frame) both sit at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION (0). If they are separate nodes, present_time currency depends on tree-order tie-breaking, which ADR-0001 s2 says is not a contract (ADR-0009 OQ-L, OQ-E). I verified only ascending distinct priorities, not tie behaviour. Confidence: medium.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 decides OQ-E: make PipelineRoot the host, so one _process advances present_time and then calls driver.frame (no tie). Failing that, ADR-0001 adds an additive PRESENTATION_EARLY constant (and PRESENTATION_LATE if ADR-0008's fallback is ever needed) so no ordering relies on tree order.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0009 requests a read-only PresentationClock.load_seq (+1 on LOADING->RUNNING and on new game). Engine-wise the `var load_seq: int: get:` read-only property is valid GDScript. ADR-0004 carries no restore marker, so is_all is ambiguous with a >256-key mass change, and the request is genuinely required. Confidence: high.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0001 adds load_seq to PresentationClock, or ADR-0004 adds a restore flag to the load-delivery ChangeBatch. Either must be Accepted before ADR-0009 (OQ-D, R9).

cross_adr.text: Both ADR-0008 (Verification and s6.2) and ADR-0001 (risk text) record frame_pre_draw as 'never fired, ordering UNVERIFIED'. A windowed 4.7.2 editor run now shows the order (all node _process, then pre_draw, then post_draw). The release export, D3D12 and Deck remain unverified. rendering/driver/threads/thread_model is not in ADR-0008's pin table. It reads 1 by default, and the emitting thread under 2 is undocumented. Confidence: high for the editor run.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 and ADR-0001 update the probe text. ADR-0008 s5 adds `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` to its pinned project settings, kept at the default 1, and checks it in the PRJ-02 boot check.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0009 relies on lints (no position writes outside placement.gd, tick_alpha only in the driver) that ADR-0010 has not specified for the full engine API surface. Writes via set_position, translate, Sprite2D.offset, and AnimationPlayer or Tween property tracks on position bypass a naive regex (see E6). ADR-0005 s1.7 already bans sort_custom only under src/sim and src/kernel, so the unstable-sort risk in src/presentation (E2) has no lint. Confidence: high.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 adds PRES lint rules: a token list for the position setter and relative-move methods, an animation-resource scan for position or offset tracks, and DET-style sort_custom ban (or packed-key rule) extended to src/presentation driver code.
